citation: First United Methodist Church at the Chicago Temple. "History." Congregational history page.
note: The successor congregation's own account of its first building, and the ONLY source reached that puts the meeting house on the north bank in its own words: 'in 1834 the growing congregation built a log cabin north of the Chicago River', and 'Four years later, Chicago's first Methodists floated the cabin across the river and rolled it on logs to its present site at the corner of Washington and Clark Streets.' Cited in this dataset for the competing reading of walker_meeting_house's location, which is NOT the reading adopted — see docs/RESEARCH/walker_meeting_house.md. Its weight is real but limited: an institution's own modern, unfootnoted history, giving a division-level location ('north of the Chicago River') rather than a position, and dating the building to 1834 where the two near-primary witnesses describe a west-bank building already standing in 1831. RE-READ IN FULL 2026-08-11 and the grade is unchanged, because there is no document under it to grade: see carries_no_document. One thing the full read adds, and it cuts against the page rather than for it — the paragraph is internally inconsistent with itself before it ever meets this project's witnesses. It has the congregation founded in 1831, worshipping in members' homes, building the cabin in 1834 and floating it across 'four years later'; the successor building on the Washington and Clark site is then dated 1845, and the standard account of the move is 1838. Nothing in the paragraph is dated to a document, so the 1834 cannot be checked against anything, which is precisely why the west-bank reading rests on the two near-primary witnesses instead. See docs/RESEARCH/evidence_tiers_round_three.md § 5.
access_notes: The page is a live CMS page and may be revised without notice, so the quotations above are recorded here verbatim so the claim survives the page changing. A Save Page Now request on 2026-08-09 produced no snapshot and archived_url was deliberately left absent rather than fabricated; a snapshot dated 2026-06-05 was found on 2026-08-11 and verified to carry both quotations character for character, so the citation is re-readable now and archived_url is recorded.
carries_no_document: Looked for what the west-bank/north-bank disagreement actually needs: a period or near-primary account of the 1834 log meeting house — a trustees' minute, a circuit rider's journal, a conference record, or a dated quotation from one. The page reprints none of those and reprints nothing at all. Its 'HISTORY' section is 500 words of modern congregational narrative running 1831 to 1924, unfootnoted end to end, with no bibliography, no further-reading link and no archive named anywhere on the site's About tree. The only quoted document on the page is a sermon of 1922 by the Rev. John Thompson, about the decision to build the present skyscraper, which is ninety years after the cabin and not about it. So this record's rung is a judgement about the congregation's own modern prose and nothing else, and it cannot rise: there is no document here for a rung to be about. Where it sends you instead is nowhere, which is itself the finding — the institution nearest to the building keeps no citable account of it that this project has been able to reach.
